correctness.rationale: For a period-\(T\) cycle, rearranging \(x_{i+1}=\varphi(x_i)+k\) gives the exact telescoping identity \(\sum_i c(x_i)=Tk\) for \(c(n)=n-\varphi(n)\). No cycle term is \(1\), so every cototient is at least \(1\). The maximum cannot be prime; for composite \(M\), the least-prime-factor argument gives \(c(M)\ge\sqrt M\). Therefore \(\sqrt M\le Tk-(T-1)=T(k-1)+1\). Equality forces every nonmaximum term to be prime and forces equality in the composite totient bound, hence \(M=q^2\) with prime \(q=T(k-1)+1\). The recurrence on prime terms then forces the entire arithmetic progression and the converse is checked algebraically. The packaged verifier replays representative cycles and extremal examples independently with integer arithmetic.

value.rationale: The theorem addresses a named structural gap in the source paper rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. It gives a sharp period-sensitive envelope for every periodic orbit of the one-step map and converts the source’s suggested prime-progression construction into a necessary-and-sufficient equality criterion. The result also yields the nontrivial relation \(T\ge(\sqrt M-1)/(k-1)\), so a large cycle maximum forces a long period. Explicit periods \(2\), \(3\), and \(4\) attain equality, demonstrating that the extremal mechanism is not merely formal.
